tldr: The paper introduces ClinicalAgent, a multi-agent system leveraging GPT-4, ReAct, and LEAST-TO-MOST reasoning to predict clinical trial outcomes, achieving 0.7908 PR-AUC—a 0.3326 improvement over standard prompt-based methods.
contributions: First multi-agent framework that elevates LLM conversational abilities with actionable intelligence for clinical trials
Integration of extensive tools, knowledge databases, and advanced reasoning technologies (ReAct, LEAST-TO-MOST) to enhance decision-making
Competitive predictive performance in clinical trial outcome prediction (0.7908 PR-AUC), with a 0.3326 improvement over the standard prompt method
methods: ClinicalAgent employs a multi-agent architecture with specialized agents: a Planning Agent that decomposes complex problems using LEAST-TO-MOST reasoning, an Efficacy Agent that assesses drug-disease relationships via DrugBank and HetioNet Knowledge Graph, a Safety Agent that evaluates drug safety from databases and historical trial outcomes, and an Enrollment Agent that uses a hierarchical transformer-based model to predict enrollment success. A Reasoning Agent aggregates subproblem solutions to make final predictions. The system integrates external tools and data sources including DrugBank, Hetionet, ClinicalTrials.gov, and LLM-generated data, alongside predictive models for enrollment difficulty and drug/disease risk estimation.
results: ClinicalAgent achieves a PR-AUC of 0.7908 in clinical trial outcome prediction, representing a 0.3326 improvement over the standard prompt-based method.
limitations: The paper primarily positions ClinicalAgent as the first LLM agent work for clinical trials but does not extensively discuss limitations of its approach. Potential limitations include reliance on GPT-4 as a commercial model, dependency on the quality and completeness of external databases (DrugBank, Hetionet, ClinicalTrials.gov), and the use of LLM-generated synthetic data that requires validation against existing sources.
